definition: In psychological assessment, metric equivalence means a measure relates its items to the underlying trait in the same way across different groups. When supported in factor invariance testing, it suggests scores can be compared across groups because the scale’s measurement pattern is consistent.

reasons: The packet states that the study found evidence of “metric” (along with configural and scalar) equivalence across sex and age groups, but it does not define what “metric equivalence” means.

Claims about how metric equivalence “relates its items to the underlying trait in the same way,” or that it “suggests scores can be compared across groups because the scale’s measurement pattern is consistent,” are not explicitly supported anywhere in the provided packet.
The definition includes conditional wording (“When supported in factor invariance testing…”) that is not itself explained in the packet beyond the existence of metric equivalence results.

The packet supports that factor invariance analyses found metric equivalence across sex and age groups, but it does not define metric equivalence as items relating to the trait in the same way across groups.

The claim that metric equivalence means scores can be compared across groups because the scale’s measurement pattern is consistent is an unsupported explanatory generalization not stated in the packet.
